title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the conclusion of a longer argument whose start is not on this sheet. It sits on the back of a Bourbaki typescript (Variétés différentielles et analytiques, majorant series), and the folder spans 1965 to about 1977.

Setting, as far as the page lets one infer it. There is a 2-category B_0 of objects C, attached to a base (A, K): plausibly a ring A and a field K, e.g. a fraction or residue field. For objects C, C' there are categories Ext(C,C'), with Ext(C) = Ext(C,C). The surrounding argument evidently shows that the Ext(C,C') behave like categories of 1-morphisms in a connected 2-groupoid, i.e. a neutral 2-gerbe.

The page then states the following.
(1) Each Ext(C) carries a canonical structure of strictly commutative Picard category: a symmetric monoidal groupoid with invertible objects and trivial self-symmetry c_{X,X} = id. Grothendieck underlines 'strictement'.
(2) Because these Picard categories are strictly commutative, the identifications Ext(C) ≃ Ext(C') obtained by transport of structure ('conjugation') along any object of Ext(C,C') do not depend on that choice, up to coherent isomorphism. So all Ext(C) can be identified with a single Picard category B. This is the 2-categorical analogue of the canonical identification of the abelian automorphism groups of the objects of a connected groupoid: the 'lien' or band of an abelian gerbe, one level up.
(3) Hence B acts on every C. Each Ext(C,C') is a torsor-category under B: a category with a B-action that is (locally) equivalent to B acting on itself.
(4) Fix a base object C. Then the 2-functor B_0 → (2-category of B-torsor-categories), C' ↦ Ext(C,C'), is an equivalence of 2-categories. This is the categorified version of: a pointed connected groupoid with abelian automorphism group G is equivalent to the groupoid of G-torsors.
(5) Functoriality. Given a base change A → A', K → K' such that the base-changed objects C_{A'} satisfy the same hypotheses, there is a morphism of Picard categories B → B'. The base-change 2-functor C ↦ C_{A'} is compatible with the actions of B and B' on the torsor-categories; the sentence trails off.

In modern terms, B_0 is classified as a neutral abelian 2-gerbe with band the Picard stack B. Its objects correspond to B-torsors, which are classified by H^1 with coefficients in B, i.e. hypercohomology of a two-term complex with π_0 B and π_1 B as cohomology. Invariants of this kind are typically of Brauer–Picard type: π_0 like a Brauer group, π_1 like a Picard group.

The name attached to B is hard to read. It is underlined, begins with 'Br', and has a long ending. The machine reading 'Breen' is possible; 'Brauer' (a 'Brauer Picard category', whose π_0 is a Brauer group and π_1 a Picard group) or another name are also conceivable.

The jottings on the previous page (Z_p, Q(i), the symbol (-1/p), TORS, B^o_c(Z)) suggest an arithmetic context with torsors over Z, but cannot be tied to this page with certainty.
errors: Step (2) needs more than strict commutativity of each Ext(C) taken separately. One also needs the natural action of Ext(C,C') by conjugation to be compatible with the Picard structures; this holds automatically when the Picard structure comes from composition in a 2-groupoid (Eckmann–Hilton type argument). Without that, only an equivalence up to a non-canonical twist is obtained.

Claim (4) is correct only if B_0 is connected, i.e. all Ext(C,C') are non-empty. Otherwise its image consists of the torsor-categories that actually occur. Essential surjectivity onto all B-torsor-categories requires B_0 to satisfy a gluing (2-stack) condition, or the torsors to be understood as globally trivial. The page leaves these hypotheses implicit.
The base-change paragraph is unfinished: the compatibility of the operations of B and B' is announced but not formulated.

ideas.what: Automorphism categories of objects in a connected 2-groupoid are strictly commutative Picard categories, canonically identified with one another, giving a single 'band' B.
ideas.modern_name: Band (lien) of an abelian 2-gerbe; Picard stack as coefficient object
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (SGA 4, Exp. XVIII, 1973) for Picard stacks; Breen (Astérisque 225, 1994) for 2-gerbes and their bands
ideas.where_published: Closely related themes appear in Pursuing Stacks (1983) and in Grothendieck's letters to Breen (1975), as far as I recall; I am unsure of the precise overlap.

ideas.what: Hom-categories Ext(C,C') are torsor-categories under B, and C' ↦ Ext(C,C') is a 2-equivalence from B_0 to B-torsor-categories.
ideas.modern_name: Classification of a neutral abelian 2-gerbe by torsors under a Picard stack (categorified torsor/gerbe correspondence)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (SGA 4 XVIII, torsors under Picard stacks); Breen (1990 'Bitorseurs', 1994)

ideas.what: Functoriality of the band B under change of base (A→A', K→K').
ideas.modern_name: Base change for Picard stacks / bands of 2-gerbes

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a categorified Galois/torsor description of a 2-category B_0 of arithmetic objects over (A,K), with a 'Picard category' B (attributed to Breen, Brauer or similar). He starts to formulate its base-change functoriality but stops. The specific B_0 and the identification of B are not determined from this page alone.
missed.quote: Si on a un chgt de base A→A', K→K', et si les C_{A'} satisfont les mêmes conditions que les C, alors on a un hom de catégories de Picard B→B' ... est compatible avec les opérations de B, B' ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, this would document Grothendieck using torsors under Picard categories (abelian 2-gerbe classification) in an arithmetic/motivic setting before Pursuing Stacks, possibly in dialogue with Breen. Mathematically, the general formalism is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is the categorified torsor classification for a strictly commutative band. It is essentially SGA 4 XVIII / Breen material and is stated, not developed. The interest is mainly historical: an early (about 1977?) use of 2-categorical torsors in Grothendieck's arithmetic notes, with an attribution to someone named 'Br...'. The specific objects C are not identifiable from this page alone.
transcription_corrections: The name after 'catégorie de Picard de' is underlined and hard to read. It may be 'Breen', but 'Brauer' or another name beginning 'Br...' is also possible.

First line: 'ont' should probably be 'sont' (the strikeout correction reads 'sont munies canoniquement d'une structure de catégorie de Picard strictement commutative', with 'commutative' crossed out after 'strictement').
'à l'homom' is better read as 'et l'homom[orphisme]' (the start of 'et' is unclear): '... et l'homomorphisme C → C_{A'} est compatible avec les opérations de B, B' ...'.
'B opère sur chaque C, et pour C, C' ∈ Ob B_0' — the image shows 'C, C'' (the first may look like C'').
